title: Original Petition for Debt Collection
text:
CAUSE NO. 2024-CV-03456

IN THE DISTRICT COURT
DALLAS COUNTY, TEXAS
224TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CRESTVIEW FINANCIAL SERVICES, LLC,
Plaintiff,
v.
EDWARD J. THOMPSON,
Defendant.

ORIGINAL PETITION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, Crestview Financial Services, LLC, Plaintiff, complaining of and about Edward J. Thompson, Defendant, and for cause of action would respectfully show unto the Court the following:

I. DISCOVERY CONTROL PLAN
1.1 Plaintiff intends to conduct discovery under Level 2 of Rule 190 of the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.

II. PARTIES
2.1 Plaintiff, Crestview Financial Services, LLC, is a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of Texas, with its principal place of business at 4500 Commerce Parkway, Suite 300, Dallas, Texas 75201. Plaintiff may be served with process through its registered agent, Capitol Corporate Services, Inc., at 100 Congress Avenue, Austin, Texas 78701.
2.2 Defendant, Edward J. Thompson, is an individual who resides at 742 Elm Street, Apt. 4B, Dallas, Texas 75202. Defendant's date of birth is August 15, 1978, and his Social Security number is 456-78-9012. Defendant may be served with process at his residence or wherever he may be found.

III. JURISDICTION AND VENUE
3.1 The amount in controversy is within the jurisdictional limits of this Court. Plaintiff seeks monetary relief of $100,000 or less, exclusive of interest and costs.
3.2 Venue is proper in Dallas County, Texas, pursuant to Section 15.002(a)(1) of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code because all or a substantial part of the events or omissions giving rise to the claim occurred in this county.

IV. FACTS
4.1 On or about March 12, 2021, Defendant executed a credit card agreement with Crestview Financial Services, LLC, account number 4567-8912-3456-7890, and was issued a credit card with a credit limit of $15,000.00.
4.2 Defendant used the credit card to make numerous purchases and cash advances, and thereby became indebted to Plaintiff in the principal amount of $12,345.67, plus accrued interest, late fees, and collection costs.
4.3 Defendant defaulted on the credit card agreement by failing to make the required monthly payments. Plaintiff sent multiple demands for payment, including a letter dated October 1, 2023, to Defendant's last known address.
4.4 Despite repeated demands, Defendant has failed and refused to pay the outstanding balance. As of the date of this petition, the total amount due and owing is $14,567.89, including principal, interest, and fees.

V. CAUSES OF ACTION
5.1 Breach of Contract – Plaintiff incorporates the foregoing paragraphs as if fully set forth herein. Defendant entered into a valid and enforceable credit card agreement with Plaintiff. Defendant breached the agreement by failing to make payments as required. Plaintiff has performed all conditions precedent to bringing this action. As a direct and proximate result of Defendant's breach, Plaintiff has suffered damages in the amount of $14,567.89.
5.2 Suit on Sworn Account – Alternatively, Plaintiff sues on a sworn account. The account is just and true, and all just and lawful offsets, payments, and credits have been allowed. The attached Exhibit A is a true and correct copy of the account statement showing the balance due.

VI. ATTORNEY'S FEES
6.1 Pursuant to Section 38.001 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, Plaintiff is entitled to recover reasonable attorney's fees. Plaintiff has retained the law firm of Bryant & Associates, PLLC, and has agreed to pay its attorneys a reasonable fee for their services. The undersigned attorney, Mark A. Bryant, Bar No. 24056789, is a partner at Bryant & Associates, PLLC, located at 2000 Main Street, Suite 1200, Dallas, Texas 75201. Plaintiff seeks an award of attorney's fees in the amount of $3,500.00, or such amount as the Court may deem just and proper.

VII. CONDITIONS PRECEDENT
7.1 All conditions precedent to Plaintiff's right to recover have been performed or have occurred.

VIII. PRAYER
WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Plaintiff prays that Defendant be cited to appear and answer herein, and that upon final trial, Plaintiff have judgment against Defendant for:
a. Actual damages in the amount of $14,567.89;
b. Pre-judgment and post-judgment interest as allowed by law;
c. Reasonable attorney's fees;
d. Costs of court; and
e. Such other and further relief to which Plaintiff may be justly entitled.

Respectfully submitted,

BRYANT & ASSOCIATES, PLLC
2000 Main Street, Suite 1200
Dallas, Texas 75201
(214) 555-0198
Email: mbryant@bryantlaw.com

BY: /s/ Mark A. Bryant
Mark A. Bryant
State Bar No. 24056789
Attorney for Plaintiff

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE
I hereby certify that a true and correct copy of the foregoing Original Petition was served on Defendant, Edward J. Thompson, on this the 15th day of March, 2024, by delivering a copy to his attorney of record, Patricia L. Henderson, at 500 Oak Street, Suite 800, Dallas, Texas 75202.

/s/ Mark A. Bryant
Mark A. Bryant

EXHIBIT A
Account Statement for Account No. 4567-8912-3456-7890
Customer: Edward J. Thompson
Balance as of March 1, 2024: $14,567.89

CITATIONS:
In support of its claims, Plaintiff relies on the following authorities: Smith v. Jones, 123 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2003); Johnson v. Garcia, 789 F. Supp. 2d 1010 (N.D. Tex. 2011). See also Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 38.001, which provides: "A person may recover reasonable attorney's fees from an individual or corporation, in addition to the amount of a valid claim and costs, if the claim is for: (1) rendered services; (2) performed labor; (3) furnished material; (4) freight or express overcharges; (5) lost or damaged freight or express; (6) killed or injured livestock; (7) a sworn account; (8) an oral or written contract; (9) a promissory note; (10) a contract for the sale of property; (11) a contract for the purchase of property; (12) a contract for the repair of personal property; or (13) a contract for the repair of real property."
